summary: Maps an input integer to a TLS error code: input 1 writes 33 into the TLS slot, inputs 2..3 write 34, and all other values leave the TLS slot untouched. Returns the TLS slot address when a code was written, otherwise returns the input cast to a pointer. Frame-path function; the TLS slot is written every call on the guarded paths.

operations.description: result = a1 cast to pointer: default return value when no error code is written.
First branch: if a1 == 1, take the error-code-33 path.
result = TLSOffsetGetter(): retrieve the TLS slot address that will hold the error code.
*result = 33: write error code 33 into the TLS slot at offset 0 of the returned pointer.
Second branch: else if a1 > 1 && a1 <= 3, take the error-code-34 path.
result = TLSOffsetGetter(): retrieve the TLS slot address for the error-code-34 write.
*result = 34: write error code 34 into the TLS slot at offset 0 of the returned pointer.
Return the TLS slot address when an error code was written, otherwise return the original a1 cast as pointer.
Invoked by ConditionalMathWithDAT005e9ad0Flag (0059168F), FloatParsingWithErrorHandling (00591BF1) and sub_596175 (00596175) to set parse/range error codes on the frame path.

unresolved: Meaning of error codes 33 and 34 and which component consumes the TLS slot is not established here.
The TLS slot write is recalcuated per frame, so external pokes to offset 0 do not persist.
